name: Southern Lalo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space (Asia-Pacific Linguistics, ANU); and Yang 2010 PhD thesis (La Trobe) covering Southern Lalo (Mangdi) phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record 'Southern Lalo' sout3210 (Glottolog's most extensive description: Yang 2010 only; links to Lexibank yanglalo-Mangdi and yangyi-SMangdi)
sources.note: Identity: 'Mangdi or Southern Lalo is a variety of Lalo recently shown to be unintelligible to all other Lalo varieties'; no ISO code; single descriptive reference (Yang 2010).

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space: subgrouping, dialectometry, and intelligibility. Asia-Pacific Linguistics A-PL 22. Canberra: ANU. 260 pp. hdl:1885/95391
sources.note: sec. 3.3 'Mangdi (MD)' pp. 44-46 (same sketch as the thesis) and sec. 5.2.1 pp. 119-121 with Table 5-3 (MD tones 55 / 11 / 33 / 44(ʔ) weakly harsh / 11(ʔ) weakly harsh; *H shorter than *3; harsh-modal contrast often neutralised utterance-medially). No statement on word stress; 'stressed' occurs only in the CW-QY (Central Lalo) sketch p. 39.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2012. Classifying Lalo languages: subgrouping, phonetic distance, and intelligibility. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 35(2): 113-137.
sources.note: Mangdi = one of seven Lalo languages (3,000 speakers, Hepai, Gengma), unintelligible to the rest; classification only, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lexibank variety pages: yanglalo 'Mangdi' (Yang 2011 wordlists, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13306849) and yangyi 'S-Mangdi' (CLDF dataset accompanying Yang 2022 Diachronica, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13220883)
sources.note: Wordlists with Chao tone letters; both map to sout3210; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2011-07-08. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: 'Southern Lalo' (tentative code svl), ISO 639-3 change request 2011-097; outcome Rejected 2012-03-28.
sources.note: Identity only: autonym lo²¹lo³³pɑ̠²¹, alt. name Menghuaren, ~3,000 speakers, Mangdi village (Hepai, Gengma) and Mengguo village (Cangyuan), N23°30' E99°20', EGIDS 6a, only a 1000-item wordlist recording exists; no phonology. The main form could not be downloaded (site timeouts).

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2011. Lalo regional varieties: 1000-item comparative wordlists (Lexibank 'yanglalo', Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13306849), incl. the Mangdi list recorded from 4 speakers in Mangyou village
sources.note: The only primary data on MD; recorded audio of the 1000-item wordlist (per ISO request 2011-097) could be examined for prominence in polysyllables if a stress statement is ever wanted; the CLDF forms themselves carry only tone letters.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2011. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, change request 2011-097 (main form, covering the proposed split of Lalo into Central/Dongshanba/Eastern/Western/Yangliu/Xuzhang/Southern/Eka)
sources.note: Companion form to the downloaded svl proposal; may cite sources for Southern Lalo not listed elsewhere (the svl form's 'published sources' field is empty). Identity only, not a stress source.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Mangdi language' (cites Yang 2010 and the 2011-097 change request only)
sources.note: Identity only: 3,000 speakers, Mangdi/Hepai/Gengma and Cangyuan; ISO request rejected; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD thesis, La Trobe University, Bundoora. 447 pp. doi:10.26181/21844209.v1
sources.note: sec. 3.3 'MD' pp. 71-74 (PDF 96-99) is the first documentation of Mangdi: (C)VTP syllable, 28 initials, 8 vowels, 3 pitch heights x harsh/modal phonation. Nothing on stress or accent anywhere for MD; the word 'stressed' appears once in the whole thesis, in the Central Lalo (CW-QY) sketch ('Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity'). p. 3: Ngwi languages incl. Lalo are 'omnisyllabic', almost every syllable carries a lexical tone.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Tone change in Lalo. In Y. Treis & R. De Busser (eds), Selected papers from the 2009 Conference of the Australian Linguistic Society.
sources.note: Acoustic/diachronic tone study of E and NW Lalo; MD not treated; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2009. Regional variation in Lalo: beyond east and west. La Trobe Papers in Linguistics 12. doi:10.26181/22202464.v1
sources.note: MD listed as a peripheral variety (Table 1); sound-change and subgrouping discussion; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2022. The phonetic tone change *high > rising: Evidence from the Ngwi dialect laboratory. Diachronica 39 (online first 2022). doi:10.1075/dia.19062.yan
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only post-2015 publication with Southern Lalo (S-Mangdi) phonetic data (CLDF dataset yangyi); a tone-change study, but could contain remarks on prominence/duration in disyllables; the sole chance of a newer statement.

sources.citation: 耿马傣族佤族自治县志 [Gengma Dai and Va Autonomous County Gazetteer]. 1995. (mentions the 'Menghua' Yi group of Hepai; per Yang 2010: 71 'no linguistic information is given')
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only Chinese record of the MD community; Yang states it contains no linguistic information, so it is listed here to close the trail, not as a likely stress source.
